title: [YouPass Collect] - Market share of three manufacturers of mobile phones: 1994 - 2004
prompt: The line graph below illustrates the proportion of mobile phone sales by three manufacturers (Motorola, Nokia and Sony Ericsson) between 1994 and 2004. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the market share, measured as a percentage of sales, of three mobile phone manufacturers, namely Motorola, Nokia, and Sony Ericsson, from 1994 to 2004.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the three brands showed distinct trends, with Nokia's market share rising significantly, Motorola's declining considerably, and Sony Ericsson's fluctuating within a narrow range. Notably, Nokia eventually overtook Motorola to become the dominant manufacturer for the majority of the period, while Sony Ericsson consistently remained the least popular brand.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: As for Motorola and Sony Ericsson, in 1994, the former held the largest market share at 32%, approximately three times higher than that of the latter, at just 11%. Motorola's figures then fell steadily over the following years, reaching a low of only 14% in 2000, before recovering slightly to 18% by 2004. Sony Ericsson, on the other hand, saw a modest rise, peaking at 15% in 1998, but then followed a similar downward path, dropping to 7% in 2003 before ending the period at 10%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding Nokia, it began the period at 21%, making it the second most popular brand behind Motorola. Its share dipped slightly to 19% in 1997, before surging dramatically over the next five years to a peak of 37% in 2002, overtaking Motorola along the way. Despite this impressive growth, Nokia's market share fell back to 30% in 2004, though it still remained the leading brand by a considerable margin.
